newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine mine tender set for July 28.
newsitem.headline: Argentine mine tender set for July 28.

text.p: An Argentine mining company will try for a second time to tender a large exploration site next to the country's biggest copper project, the firm said Thursday.

Yacimientos Mineros Aguas de Dionisio (YMAD) has invited 19 "top line" international companies to bid July 28 for the site and will not accept other offers, YMAD general manager Carlos Maldonado told Reuters.
YMAD agreed to grant the prospect to Eastcan Mining Ltd after an earlier open tender, but the deal fell through when the Canadian firm failed to find guarantors for its bid.
Eastcan had offered to pay YMAD $10 million on signing the deal, make $3 million in conditional paymants, and invest $20 million exploring the site in northwestern Argentina.
The area is near the $1 billion Bajo de la Alumbrera copper and gold project, which is due to be the world's biggest ever base metal start up when it begins production in August or September.
Alumbrera's partners -- it is held 50 percent by Australia's MIM Holdings Ltd, and 25 percent each by Australia's North Ltd and Canada's Rio Algom Ltd -- bid for the new site in the first tender.
Minera Alumbrera president Peter Freund has described the area as of "modest exploration potential".
YMAD, which also owns the site of Bajo de la Alumbrera, is owned by Catamarca province, Tucuman National University, and the government of Argentina.
